title: Stripe Checkout's success and cancel URLs 404 — every library that pays lands on "This page could not be found"
what: startCheckout builds successUrl/cancelUrl as `${BILLING_RETURN_URL}/t/<slug>/billing?checkout=success`. The web app has exactly one billing route, `/[locale]/t/[slug]/billing` (4 path segments, locale mandatory). `/t/<slug>/billing` is 3 segments, there is no root-level catch-all (apps/web/app contains only `[locale]`, `api`, page.tsx, not-found.tsx), no Next middleware, and next.config.mjs rewrites only `/_assets/*`, `/lbr-api/*` and `/admin/*`. Neither web caller ever supplies `returnPath` (PlanGrid.tsx:109-115 and ChoosePlanScreen.tsx:62-68 send only planSlug + interval), so the locale-less fallback on line 302 is always what Stripe receives.
impact: The single most expensive moment in the product — a library has just entered a card and paid — ends on a 404 page. The subscription is real and the charge is real, so the librarian believes the payment failed and either retries (see billing-03: a second Stripe subscription) or emails support. First impression of the paid product is a broken page.
evidence:
EXECUTED. Booted the existing production build (`next start -p 3999`) and requested both paths:
  /t/demo/billing?checkout=success -> 404   (body contains "could not be found")
  /el/t/demo/billing               -> 307   (redirect to login, i.e. the route exists)
Route table confirms it: `grep -o '"/[^"]*billing[^"]*"' apps/web/.next/types/routes.d.ts` yields exactly one entry, "/[locale]/t/[slug]/billing".
fix: Prefix the locale in the return path: resolve the caller's locale (pass it from the client, or default to `el`) and build `${base}/${locale}/t/${slug}/billing?checkout=success`. Apply the same fix to openCustomerPortal's return_url (billing.service.ts:335-340), which has the identical defect. Add an assertion in the checkout spec that the generated successUrl matches a real Next route.

title: With STRIPE_DRIVER=fake — what every production template writes today — the webhook verifies signatures against a hardcoded secret published in this repo
what: FakeStripeDriver hardcodes `private secret = 'fake-webhook-secret-for-dev'` and only tests ever call setSecret(). billing.module.ts:22-28 selects the driver purely on `STRIPE_DRIVER`, and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is never handed to the fake driver. POST /webhooks/stripe is unauthenticated by design and, per SystemModeMiddleware ALWAYS_PASS (system-mode.middleware.ts:44), bypasses maintenance/read-only mode; OriginCheckMiddleware allows a missing Origin (origin-check.middleware.ts:41). So while the fake driver is in place, the signature check is satisfiable by anyone. `.env.prod.example:69` sets STRIPE_DRIVER=fake, `scripts/ensure-env.sh:100` writes it as the default, and `infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml:65` defaults it to fake — and docs/billing-go-live.md tells the operator to flip the master switch from the admin panel, which requires no .env change at all, so enforcement can be turned on while this driver is still serving.
impact: Any internet host can rewrite any tenant's subscription row: grant themselves Institutional, or set another library to canceled/past_due. The victim's Stripe customer id is not even a secret in this mode — FakeStripeDriver.createCustomer mints `cus_fake_<tenantId>` and GET /t/:slug/billing returns both tenantId and stripeCustomerId to the tenant's own admin. The forged rows persist and become the truth the moment billing is enabled. Signature minting is also unlimited, so stripe_webhook_events grows without bound.
evidence:
EXECUTED, twice.
(1) Unit-level: constructing FakeStripeDriver exactly as billing.module.ts does, with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_the_operator_set_a_real_one in the environment, prints `driver secret in use : fake-webhook-secret-for-dev` and accepts an event signed with that literal.
(2) End-to-end over HTTP against the audit Postgres, booting the real AppModule and POSTing to /webhooks/stripe with no credential of any kind, only `signFakeWebhook(body,'fake-webhook-secret-for-dev')`: HTTP 200, and the control plane moved from
  libwf-be65e9 | starter | active | (null)
to
  libwf-be65e9 | institutional | active | sub_audit
with stripe_webhook_events showing the event processed=t, error=null. An event signed with any other secret returned 400.
fix: Two independent changes. (a) Make the fake driver refuse to verify anything outside development: throw from its constructor when `loadEnv().nodeEnv !== 'development'`, or require STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and use it instead of the literal. (b) Refuse to boot when the toggle can enforce but the driver is fake — extend the main.ts guard (which already refuses RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED in production) to reject `nodeEnv==='production' && stripeDriver!=='real'`, and have PlatformSettingsService.setBillingEnabled throw rather than log a warning (platform-settings.service.ts:60-66) in that state.

title: Every plan change opens a NEW Stripe subscription and abandons the old one — an upgrade double-charges the library, forever
what: startCheckout's only guard against an existing subscription is `plan.id === sub.planId && sub.status === 'active'` (line 285). Any other plan goes to `stripe.checkout.sessions.create({ mode:'subscription', ... })` (stripe-real.driver.ts:68-78), which always creates an additional subscription for that customer — it never modifies an existing one. Nothing in the codebase cancels or updates the previous subscription: the StripeDriver interface (stripe-driver.ts:93-110) has no `updateSubscription`/`subscriptions.update` and no proration parameter anywhere in the repo (`grep -rn proration_behavior apps` returns nothing). syncStripeSubscription then overwrites `stripeSubscriptionId` with the new id (line 617), so the old subscription's id is erased from our database entirely and cancelAtPeriodEnd (line 359) can only ever reach the newest one.
impact: A Community library upgrading to Municipal is charged €39 AND €79 every month, indefinitely. A library 'downgrading' from Municipal to Community adds €39 on top of the €79 it is still paying. Neither the library nor an operator can see the orphan — it exists only in Stripe. Cancelling from the app stops the newest subscription and leaves the older one billing. This is charge-back and refund territory on the first paying customers.
evidence:
EXECUTED against the audit control plane. Applied sub_A (community, active), then a second subscription sub_B (central, active) for the same customer, exactly as a second Checkout would produce:
  after checkout created sub_B while sub_A lives  plan=central  status=active  stripeSub=sub_B
  rows anywhere still referencing sub_A: 0
Read-only for the Stripe side: `mode:'subscription'` Checkout creates a new subscription; the repo contains no call that would replace the old one.
fix: Do not route plan changes through Checkout. When `sub.stripeSubscriptionId` is set, call `stripe.subscriptions.update(id, { items:[{ id: <item>, price: newPriceId }], proration_behavior:'create_prorations' })` through a new driver method and let the resulting `customer.subscription.updated` webhook do the sync; reserve Checkout for the first subscription only. Until that lands, block startCheckout with a 400 whenever `sub.stripeSubscriptionId != null`.

title: No VAT anywhere in the billing path — Greek libraries cannot pay against the receipt, and ~24% of every euro collected is owed regardless
what: createCheckoutSession sets mode, customer, line_items, urls, client_reference_id and `customer_update`. It does NOT set `automatic_tax: { enabled: true }`, `tax_id_collection: { enabled: true }`, or `billing_address_collection: 'required'`. `customer_update:{name:'auto',address:'auto'}` is the companion parameter Stripe requires alongside automatic_tax; on its own it collects nothing. Stripe therefore charges the Price amount with no tax line and issues a receipt with no VAT and no customer VAT number. The control plane already has the columns for this — billing_accounts.taxId, taxCountry, addressLine1..country (schema.prisma:574-580) — and no code path anywhere writes them: ensureStripeCustomer (billing.service.ts:746-780) sets only billingEmail and billingName. The marketing site's own build lint forbids the words ΦΠΑ, ΑΦΜ and τιμολόγιο (apps/site/build.ts:180, reason: 'The business is not registered and nothing is trademarked'), so the advertised '390 €' carries no statement of whether VAT is included or excluded.
impact: Two separate injuries. (1) The customers are Greek municipalities and δημόσιες βιβλιοθήκες; their accounting departments cannot book a payment without a compliant invoice carrying the supplier's ΑΦΜ and the ΦΠΑ line. A Stripe card receipt with neither cannot be paid from a public budget — the deals stall after the card is entered. (2) A price advertised with no VAT statement is treated as VAT-inclusive, so of a €390 annual sale roughly €75 is owed to AADE out of money already booked as revenue; every tier is ~19.4% less profitable than the pricing model assumes. Neither problem is detectable from inside the app.
evidence: READ. `grep -rn 'automatic_tax|tax_id_collection|billing_address_collection|proration_behavior|taxCountry' apps/api/src apps/web/app apps/site packages/db-control/prisma/schema.prisma` returns exactly one hit — the unused schema column `packages/db-control/prisma/schema.prisma:575: taxCountry String?`. docs/billing-go-live.md contains no occurrence of tax, VAT or ΦΠΑ; its whole configuration surface is eight price ids, a webhook URL and four env vars.
fix: Enable Stripe Tax on the account, then set `automatic_tax:{enabled:true}`, `tax_id_collection:{enabled:true}` and `billing_address_collection:'required'` on the Checkout session, and mirror the resulting `customer.tax_ids` / address back into billing_accounts on the customer.updated webhook. Decide and state on both the pricing page and the plan cards whether the figure is πλέον ΦΠΑ or συμπ. ΦΠΑ, and add that step to docs/billing-go-live.md. This is gated on the company actually being registered with an ΑΦΜ.

title: A subscription whose first payment never succeeded (`incomplete`) is granted the full paid plan for 7 days, repeatably
what: The status map sends Stripe's `incomplete` to our `past_due` (line 567). `incomplete` is the state of a subscription whose INITIAL invoice has not been paid — the customer abandoned 3-D Secure, or the first charge was declined. Because localStatus is past_due, the write on line 630 arms `graceUntil = now + BILLING_GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS` (default 7), and the effective-plan resolver deliberately keeps full feature access for past_due inside its grace window (effective-plan.service.ts:175). The grace window is meant to protect an established payer whose card lapsed; it is applied here to someone who has never paid at all. Nothing prevents the same tenant starting checkout again once the incomplete subscription expires.
impact: Anyone who reaches Checkout and abandons the card step gets a week of the most expensive tier for nothing — and can renew it indefinitely. In the probe below the tenant went from max_books 5,000 to 400,000 and api_access false to true. Beyond the lost revenue, a library that bulk-imports 300,000 titles during a free window is left permanently over quota when the window closes, with QuotaService refusing writes and no supported way back.
evidence:
EXECUTED with BILLING_ENABLED forced on through PlatformSettingsService, against the audit control plane:
  BEFORE  plan= starter        max_books= 5000    api_access= false
  row after incomplete: institutional past_due grace= 2026-08-30T09:54:32.915Z
  AFTER   plan= institutional  max_books= 400000  api_access= true
  => paid entitlement granted with ZERO payment for 7.0 days
fix: Map `incomplete` to a status that grants nothing (add an `incomplete` value to SubscriptionStatus, or map it to `canceled`) and arm graceUntil only when transitioning from a previously-paid state. A grace window should require evidence of at least one settled invoice.

title: The stale-replay guard is inert for exactly the events that matter — a replayed mid-cycle plan change silently reverts the plan
what: The STRIPE-RETRY-STALE-REPLAY guard rejects a payload only when `nextPeriodStart < existing.currentPeriodStart` — strictly earlier. A mid-cycle plan change does not move the billing period: Stripe keeps `current_period_start` and prorates. So both the old and the new `customer.subscription.updated` carry the same period start, the guard's condition is false, and whichever event is applied last wins. The retry sweep (jobs/stripe-retry.job.ts:52-60) re-dispatches stored payloads ordered by receivedAt, and Stripe itself does not guarantee delivery order; nothing else compares `event.created` (the webhook envelope's timestamp is not persisted or consulted anywhere).
impact: A library upgrades to Municipal, an older Community event is redelivered or swept, and their plan quietly reverts to Community while Stripe bills Municipal. The reverse is equally possible after a downgrade. The event is logged as processed with no error, so the only symptom is a librarian hitting a 402 on a plan they paid to leave.
evidence:
EXECUTED. Same subscription id, same current_period_start throughout:
  after annual community sub_A               plan=community  status=active  stripeSub=sub_A
  after upgrade to municipal (same period)   plan=municipal   status=active  stripeSub=sub_A
  after stale replay of the community event  plan=community   status=active  stripeSub=sub_A
No 'ignoring stale subscription event' warning was emitted — the guard did not fire.
fix: Persist the event envelope's `created` timestamp (and/or Stripe's `Subscription.metadata`-free monotonic proxy) on the subscriptions row and reject any event older than the last one applied for the same subscription id, instead of comparing period starts.

title: A webhook payload with a null `customer` rewrites an arbitrary tenant's subscription (Prisma turns null into IS NULL)
what: `controlDb.billingAccount.findFirst({ where: { stripeCustomerId: payload.customer } })` is called with no validation that `payload.customer` is a non-empty string. Prisma renders a null filter value as `stripeCustomerId IS NULL`, which matches every tenant that has never been through Checkout — i.e. essentially the entire tenant base, since signup creates a billing_accounts row with a null customer id. findFirst then returns whichever row the planner emits first and the handler rewrites that tenant's plan, billingMode and stripeSubscriptionId. handleStripeSubscriptionDeleted (line 652) has the identical lookup, and its own stale-delete guard passes trivially for a victim whose stripeSubscriptionId is null, so a null-customer delete downgrades an arbitrary tenant to starter/canceled.
impact: Combined with billing-02 this is arbitrary-tenant takeover with a single request and no need to know any identifier at all. Independently it is a correctness hole: any malformed or partially-captured payload replayed by the sweep mutates a tenant chosen at random by the query planner, and the log line names the right subscription with the wrong library.
evidence:
EXECUTED. `findFirst({where:{stripeCustomerId:null}})` returned tenant cmt5mhy41dd101750da0616e3d7 (owner@aud-072bfa.test), an unrelated library. Feeding syncStripeSubscription a payload with `customer: null`:
  victim before: starter active
  victim after : institutional active sub_nullcustomer
fix: Guard at the top of syncStripeSubscription, handleStripeSubscriptionDeleted and tenantForSubscriptionInvoice: `if (typeof payload.customer !== 'string' || !payload.customer) { log; return; }`. Prefer resolving the tenant from `client_reference_id` (already set on every Checkout session, stripe-real.driver.ts:74) with the customer id as a fallback.

title: A webhook that fails during a database outage is lost permanently — 200 is returned to Stripe and no durable row exists for the sweep to rescue
what: The durable `stripe_webhook_events` insert is best-effort: its `.catch()` on line 83 logs a warning and continues. The handler then dispatches; on failure it logs, attempts an update of the row that was never written (swallowed by `.catch(() => undefined)`), deletes the Redis lock, and returns `{ received: true }` with HTTP 200 (the @HttpCode(200) on line 48 applies to every non-throwing return). Stripe treats 200 as final and never redelivers. The retry sweep can only find rows in stripe_webhook_events (stripe-retry.job.ts:52). The comment on line 118 — 'Drop the Redis lock so a Stripe retry can re-attempt' — describes a retry that cannot happen, because we already told Stripe the event was received.
impact: The one failure mode both recovery mechanisms are built for — a Postgres blip — is the exact case where both are unavailable, because the insert and the dispatch fail together. Subscription state silently diverges from Stripe: a cancellation never applied, a payment failure never recorded, a paid upgrade never provisioned, with no error row, no alert, and no way to know which events were lost.
evidence: READ, stripe-webhook.controller.ts:73-123. The upsert's failure path is a warn-and-continue; the dispatch catch block ends in `return { received: true }` at line 123 with no rethrow and no status change. Cross-checked against the sweep's query (stripe-retry.job.ts:52-60), which selects only from stripe_webhook_events.
fix: If the durable insert fails, do not proceed — rethrow so Nest returns a 5xx and Stripe retries. Likewise, on a dispatch failure where the error row could not be written, return non-2xx. A 200 must mean 'this event is durably ours'.

title: ensureStripeCustomer races itself — a duplicate Stripe customer means the library is charged while staying on the free plan
what: Read-then-create with a network call in between and no lock, no transaction and no Stripe Idempotency-Key: findUnique (line 747) → stripe.customers.create (line 754) → update/create (lines 761-777). Two concurrent requests — a double-clicked Subscribe button, or the chooser and the billing page in two tabs — both see no customer, both create one, and the second write wins. The user completes Checkout against whichever customer their session used; if that is the loser, every subsequent webhook for it fails the `findFirst({stripeCustomerId})` lookup at line 534 and returns after logging 'Webhook: no BillingAccount for customer …'. `client_reference_id` carries the tenantId on every session (stripe-real.driver.ts:74) and would resolve this, but nothing reads it — the controller treats checkout.session.completed as a deliberate no-op (stripe-webhook.controller.ts:144-147).
impact: The library's card is charged every month by a live Stripe subscription that our database has never heard of. They stay on the free plan, hit Starter quotas, and see 'no active paid subscription to cancel' if they try to stop it. Recovery requires someone to notice a warn-level log line and repair the customer id by hand. There is no reconciliation job that would ever catch it.
evidence: READ, billing.service.ts:746-780 — no transaction, no unique constraint on the create path, no idempotency key on any Stripe write in stripe-real.driver.ts (`grep -n idempotency apps/api/src` returns nothing).
fix: Pass a stable Stripe Idempotency-Key (`customer:<tenantId>`) to customers.create, and make the local write an upsert inside a transaction so a losing racer adopts the winner's id. Additionally, handle checkout.session.completed by reconciling `client_reference_id` → `customer`, which repairs the mismatch even when it happens.

title: Nothing reconciles the local price catalogue with Stripe, and the go-live verification step passes on the seeded placeholders
what: PATCH /admin/plans/:slug writes stripePriceId and stripeAnnualPriceId as bare optional strings (UpdatePlanDto lines 34-49). There is no format check (`price_` prefix), no rejection of the `price_seed_*` placeholders, no call to Stripe to confirm the Price exists, no check that its currency and unit_amount match the plan's `currency`/`monthlyPriceCents`/`annualPriceCents`, no check that the Price's recurring interval matches the column it is being stored in, and no guard against putting the SAME id in both columns. Separately, `hasStripePrice`/`hasStripeAnnualPrice` are computed as `!!p.stripePriceId` (billing.service.ts:116-117), and the seed ships non-null placeholders for every paid plan — so the verification command docs/billing-go-live.md ends with, which asks the operator to confirm `hasStripeAnnualPrice: true`, returns true on a completely unconfigured database.
impact: The document's single mechanical safeguard is vacuous: it reports success on the seed data it was written to catch. A monthly id pasted into the annual column bills €39/month to a library that clicked '390 € a year'; a bad id 500s at Checkout; a mismatched amount means the advertised price and the charged price differ with nothing to detect it. All of these survive every check the product performs.
evidence:
EXECUTED. Fresh seeded control plane:
  starter|stripe|0|(null)|price_seed_starter|(null)|EUR
  community|stripe|3900|39000|price_seed_community|price_seed_community_annual|EUR
  … all five paid plans carry non-null placeholders, so hasStripePrice and hasStripeAnnualPrice are both true for every one of them.
Also EXECUTED: `UPDATE plans SET "stripePriceId"='price_dup', "stripeAnnualPriceId"='price_dup' WHERE slug='community'` → UPDATE 1, both unique indexes satisfied, no error.
fix: In the PATCH handler, call `stripe.prices.retrieve(id)` and reject unless it is active, its currency equals plan.currency, its unit_amount equals the matching *PriceCents, and its recurring.interval matches the column. Reject any id equal to another column's on the same plan and any id matching /^price_seed_/. Change hasStripePrice to mean 'verified against Stripe' rather than 'non-null', so the go-live check has something to fail on.

title: The billing page's downgrade-to-free button sends the library to Stripe Checkout, and Starter's placeholder price can never be removed
what: PlanGrid's button chain is isCurrent → isManual → !hasStripePrice → upgrade(). It has no free-plan branch: unlike ChoosePlanScreen (ChoosePlanScreen.tsx:55-59, which routes monthlyPriceCents===0 to POST /billing/select), PlanGrid calls POST /billing/checkout for Starter too. Server-side, startCheckout only rejects a missing priceId (billing.service.ts:276) — and Starter's is not missing, because the CHECK constraint `plans_stripe_price_matches_mode` (migrations/20260822140000_repricing/migration.sql:35-41) requires every billingMode='stripe' plan to carry a non-null stripePriceId, and the seed makes Starter stripe-billed with `price_seed_starter`. docs/billing-go-live.md line 'Starter is free and gets no Price' plus 'every one of them must be replaced' is therefore not executable.
impact: There is no working way to move from a paid plan back to the free tier. The button either 500s (Stripe: no such price price_seed_starter) or, if the operator invents a €0 Price to satisfy the constraint, opens a second €0 subscription while the paid one keeps billing (billing-03). Meanwhile the free plan permanently carries a fake Stripe price id that no audit of the plans table can distinguish from a real one.
evidence: EXECUTED: `UPDATE plans SET "stripePriceId"=NULL WHERE slug='starter';` → ERROR: new row for relation "plans" violates check constraint "plans_stripe_price_matches_mode". READ: PlanGrid.tsx:236-249 has no `isFree` branch in the action chain, while ChoosePlanScreen.tsx:55-59 does.
fix: Give PlanGrid the same free-plan branch as ChoosePlanScreen (POST /billing/select), and have selectPlan cancel any live Stripe subscription first. Reject planSlug values whose monthlyPriceCents is 0 in startCheckout. Relax the CHECK to allow a stripe-billed plan with monthlyPriceCents=0 to hold a null price id, so Starter can be honest about having none.

title: Admin 'set plan' onto the manual plan leaves the Stripe subscription live and simultaneously removes the tenant's ability to cancel it
what: applyAdminPlanChange writes planId, billingMode (taken from the target plan) and status='active', and deliberately leaves stripeSubscriptionId untouched — the comment on lines 417-418 says Stripe remains the source of truth for that subscription's lifecycle, but no code ever cancels it. Once billingMode is 'manual', cancelAtPeriodEnd throws 'Your library is billed manually' (line 363) and openCustomerPortal throws 'there is no self-serve portal to open' (line 329), and the web UI hides BillingActions entirely for manual mode (billing/page.tsx:120-129).
impact: Moving a paying library onto a contract or on-prem arrangement — the normal reason an operator touches this endpoint — leaves the card being charged every month with the self-serve stop button removed from the product. The only remedy is someone remembering to cancel it in the Stripe dashboard by hand; nothing in the app, the audit log or the doc prompts them to.
evidence: READ, billing.service.ts:410-419 versus 359-367 and 322-331. There is no call to cancelSubscriptionAtPeriodEnd on the admin path, and the StripeDriver interface offers no other way to stop a subscription.
fix: When applyAdminPlanChange moves a tenant with a live stripeSubscriptionId onto a manual plan, cancel that subscription through the driver (immediately or at period end, as a parameter) and null the id; refuse the change if the cancel call fails, so it cannot half-apply.

title: The founding-offer procedure the go-live doc mandates cannot be carried out, and the term it creates expires silently
where: docs/billing-go-live.md ('Founding-offer libraries must be on billingMode = manual with paidUntil twelve months out')
what: billingMode is never settable on its own: every write derives it from the chosen plan (billing.service.ts:241 selectPlan, :415 applyAdminPlanChange, :618 syncStripeSubscription, auth/signup.service.ts:181). The only plan with billingMode='manual' is `on-prem-enterprise`. applyManualPayment refuses unless billingMode is already 'manual' (line 452). So making one of the five launch libraries 'manual' means moving them to on-prem-enterprise, which (a) grants 1,000,000,000 on every quota rather than the tier they were promised, and (b) has monthlyPriceCents = 0, which getDesktopAccess reads as a free plan and blocks — `if (sub.plan.monthlyPriceCents <= 0) return { allowed:false, reason:'free-plan' }` (billing.service.ts:186-188). Separately, nothing anywhere watches paidUntil: `grep -rn paidUntil apps/api/src` shows it read only by the effective-plan SQL and written only by applyManualPayment; there is no job, no email, no admin list of upcoming expiries.
impact: The twelve-months-free cohort — the entire Greek go-to-market — cannot be configured as documented. If they are put on on-prem-enterprise they lose the desktop app the offer includes. Whatever is done, on the day paidUntil passes the effective-plan join drops (effective-plan.service.ts:180) and all five libraries fall to Starter caps mid-morning with no warning to them and no notification to the operator.
evidence: EXECUTED: the plans table shows on-prem-enterprise as the only manual plan, monthlyPriceCents=0, and its plan_feature_values are 1000000000 across every integer feature with every boolean true. READ: desktop-access.spec.ts covers free/paid/trialing/past_due/canceled/paused but has no manual-plan case (`grep -n 'it(' apps/api/src/desktop/desktop-access.spec.ts`).
fix: Base the desktop entitlement on billingMode/plan tier rather than `monthlyPriceCents > 0`. Allow billingMode to be set per-subscription independently of the plan (an admin flag), so a library can sit on Municipal with manual billing. Add a scheduled job that warns the operator — and the library — 30 and 7 days before paidUntil lapses, and an admin view listing expiring manual terms.

title: `stripeReady` is computed for the admin UI and no UI ever reads it — the only signal that production is running the fake driver is a log line
what: subscriptionsStatus() returns `stripeReady` with the comment 'the admin UI can warn that checkout won't really charge', and setBillingEnabled logs a warning in the same situation (lines 60-66). Neither reaches a human: `grep -rn stripeReady apps/web` returns nothing, and SubscriptionsToggle.tsx renders only billingEnabled, source and awaitingChoice (its warning banner at line 102 is about the plan chooser). Nothing refuses the flip.
impact: An operator who enables subscriptions from the admin panel — which docs/billing-go-live.md explicitly instructs them to do, and which requires no .env change — while STRIPE_DRIVER is still fake sees a completely normal screen. Libraries then click Subscribe, are redirected to their own billing page with `?checkout=success` appended by the fake driver (stripe-fake.driver.ts:54), and are never charged. Revenue is zero and the UI says everything worked.
evidence: EXECUTED: `grep -rn 'stripeReady' apps/web apps/api/src` returns four hits, all inside platform-settings.service.ts. READ: SubscriptionsToggle.tsx:95-105.
fix: Render stripeReady as a blocking banner on the Subscriptions page and disable the enable-toggle while it is false, or make setBillingEnabled throw outside development when the driver is not real (see billing-02).

title: The go-live doc's webhook step can be completed successfully while nothing is actually wired: the one event a reader would naturally subscribe to is a deliberate no-op
what: Step 3 says: point the endpoint at /webhooks/stripe, 'Send a test event and confirm a 200'. It never lists which events the endpoint must be subscribed to. The controller acts on customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted and invoice.payment_succeeded/failed, and explicitly ignores checkout.session.completed — the event whose name most obviously matches 'someone subscribed'. Every unlisted type falls to the default branch and is logged at debug. The doc also never mentions saving a Customer Portal configuration in the Stripe dashboard, without which billingPortal.sessions.create fails for every tenant that clicks 'Open portal'.
impact: An operator who subscribes the endpoint to checkout.session.completed alone gets a 200 on the test event, sees a green tick in Stripe, and ships. Libraries then pay and nothing provisions: no plan change, no status, no grace handling — and the failure is silent because the ignored event is logged at debug level. The portal button 500s on first use for everyone.
evidence: READ. docs/billing-go-live.md step 3 in full: 'Stripe → Developers → Webhooks → https://app.libriant.com/webhooks/stripe. Send a test event and confirm a 200 in dc logs api.' No event list, no portal configuration step. stripe-webhook.controller.ts:144-147 returns immediately for checkout.session.completed; :148-149 logs unknown types at debug.
fix: List the five required event types verbatim in the doc and add a startup/health check that reports which of them have been seen at least once. Add the Customer Portal configuration step. Consider handling checkout.session.completed properly rather than relying on ordering (it also fixes billing-09).

title: The doc's own pre-flight check — 'check no existing tenant is already over its cap' — cannot be performed in production
what: The doc tells the operator to verify no tenant is over its cap before enabling enforcement, and in the very next bullet concedes that GET /t/:slug/plan/usage sits behind NonProductionOnlyGuard. That guard is the first in the chain (plan-demo.controller.ts:72), so the endpoint 404s in production. There is no admin-side equivalent — `grep -rn 'plan/usage' apps` finds only that controller — and no bulk query, so the doc asks for a check the product does not offer and supplies no SQL to do it by hand.
impact: Enforcement is switched on blind. Every tenant that grew past a Starter cap during the free period discovers it as a 402 in the middle of a task on Monday morning, with no usage screen to explain why (the same guard hides that from them too).
evidence: READ. plan-demo.controller.ts:68-72 — 'NonProductionOnlyGuard MUST run first so prod requests 404 before TenantGuard' — followed by @Get('plan/usage') at line 86. No other route serves usage counters.
fix: Add an admin endpoint that lists every tenant whose current counters exceed the caps of the plan they would be enforced against, and reference it from the doc as the pre-flight command. Open the tenant-facing usage endpoint in production so a librarian who is refused can see why.

title: The payment-failure banner is hardcoded English on a Greek-first product
what: The past_due banner's title is translated (t('billing.errors.paymentFailed')) but its body is a literal template string: `Your plan stays active until ${fmtDate(snapshot.graceUntil)}.` Every other string on the page goes through the catalog.
impact: The one sentence that tells a Greek librarian how long they have to fix a failed card — the highest-stakes message in the billing screen — appears in English regardless of locale, so the deadline may simply not be read.
fix: Move it to the catalog as billing.errors.paymentFailedGrace with a {date} parameter, in both el and en.

title: No test exercises the Stripe webhook over HTTP, so the raw-body plumbing every signature depends on is unverified in CI
what: stripe-webhook.controller.spec.ts is a unit test that calls handle() directly with a hand-built `req.rawBody` and a mocked driver, so it never exercises Express body parsing, the `rawBody: true` NestFactory option in main.ts:27, the middleware chain, or the Caddy /webhooks/* route. The integration project contains no billing spec at all (`grep -rl 'billing|stripe' apps/api/test/integration` matches only desktop-access, import-api, admin-audit and admin-role-guard, none of which touch the webhook).
impact: A regression that stops populating req.rawBody — a body-parser change, a middleware reordering, an upgrade — would pass every test and only surface as 100% of Stripe webhooks returning 400 'Raw body unavailable — server misconfigured' in production, with subscription state frozen and Stripe giving up after three days.
evidence: EXECUTED: I added a throwaway integration spec that boots the real AppModule and POSTs a signed body over HTTP; it passed (200), confirming rawBody works today — and that no such coverage previously existed. The spec has been removed.
fix: Keep a permanent integration spec that POSTs a correctly-signed event over HTTP and asserts a 200 plus the resulting subscription row, and a second asserting 400 for a bad signature.
